text: Auntie, please take one paracetamol 500mg tablet every six hours if you have fever, but not more than eight tablets a day.
This amoxicillin is an antibiotic, so finish the whole seven-day course even if you feel better by day three.
Uncle, your metformin must be taken after breakfast and after dinner, never on an empty stomach.
Shake the Ventolin inhaler first, breathe out fully, then press once while you take a slow, deep breath in.
If you forget your amlodipine in the morning, take it when you remember, but don't double up the next day.
Once opened, your insulin pen can stay at room temperature for four weeks, but keep the spare pens in the fridge.
Some people get a dry, tickly cough with perindopril. If it keeps bothering you, let the doctor know.
Take the omeprazole thirty minutes before breakfast with plain water, so it can protect your stomach properly.
Prednisolone should be taken in the morning with food. Please don't stop it suddenly without asking us first.
Ibuprofen can irritate the stomach lining, so always eat something before you take it.
Warfarin is a blood thinner, auntie, so take it at the same time every evening, around six o'clock.
With doxycycline, stay upright for at least half an hour after swallowing and drink a full glass of water.
Cetirizine may make you a little drowsy, so it's better to take it at night before bed.
The azithromycin is only for three days, one tablet a day, and you can take it with or without food.
Gliclazide can bring your sugar down too low, so never skip lunch after taking your morning dose.
After every puff of the budesonide inhaler, rinse your mouth with water and spit it out.
Clopidogrel helps prevent another stroke, so please don't stop it on your own, even for a few days.
Mix one sachet of oral rehydration salts into 200ml of clean drinking water and sip it slowly.
For your son, the paracetamol syrup is 5ml every six hours whenever his temperature goes above thirty-eight.
Losartan is for your blood pressure. One 50mg tablet every morning, at about the same time each day.
Atorvastatin works best at night, so take it after dinner, and tell us if you notice any unusual muscle aches.
Can you show me how you inject your insulin? I'd like to check your technique before you go home.
Rotate your injection sites around the tummy, keeping at least two finger-widths away from the belly button.
Your Panadol is only for pain or fever, so there's no need to take it on days you feel fine.
Please don't take Uphamol together with cold and flu tablets, because many of them already contain paracetamol.
With the spacer, press the inhaler once, then take five slow breaths through the mouthpiece before the next puff.
If your daughter vomits within half an hour of the amoxicillin, you can give the same dose again.
Keep the salbutamol syrup away from direct sunlight, and discard it one month after opening.
The doctor has increased your amlodipine from 5mg to 10mg, so that's now two tablets every morning.
This is a new prescription, metformin 500mg twice daily. Some tummy upset in the first week is quite common.
Your insulin dose tonight is twelve units before dinner. Please check your sugar first and write it in the book.
Don't worry if the ibuprofen doesn't work in ten minutes; give it about an hour to take effect.
Uncle, the warfarin tablets come in different colours for different strengths, so always check the colour before taking.
While you're on warfarin, avoid taking any traditional or herbal remedies without checking with the pharmacist.
Omeprazole is usually for four weeks only. After that, the doctor will decide whether you still need it.
If you miss a dose of doxycycline, take it as soon as you remember, unless the next dose is nearly due.
These prednisolone tablets are 5mg each. You'll take six tablets every morning for five days, then stop.
Your inhaler is almost empty when the counter shows twenty. Please get a refill from the pharmacy before it runs out.
The brown inhaler is your preventer, used every morning and night. The blue one is only for when you're breathless.
Take gliclazide just before breakfast, and always carry some sweets in case your sugar drops.
Losartan may make you feel slightly dizzy for the first few days, so stand up slowly from bed.
Uncle, you can stop the cetirizine once the rash has gone, no need to finish the whole strip.
For the gout pain, take ibuprofen 400mg three times a day after meals, for up to five days.
Perindopril is taken once in the morning. If your lips or face feel puffy, stop it and come in.
Please bring all your medicine boxes next visit, so the doctor can check exactly what you're taking.
The oral rehydration salts taste a bit salty, but try to finish one glass after each loose stool.
Auntie, the clopidogrel may cause easy bruising, which is expected. Just let us know if it's getting worse.
You don't need to cut the amlodipine tablet. Just swallow it whole with water.
Atorvastatin is for your cholesterol, not your blood pressure, so please take both as prescribed.
After a hypo, eat three sweets or drink half a glass of juice, then recheck your sugar in fifteen minutes.
Your son can have the cetirizine syrup, 5ml once at night, for the itchy skin.
For the TB treatment, take all the tablets together on an empty stomach, one hour before breakfast.
TB medicine can turn your urine orange-red. That's normal, so please don't stop the tablets because of it.
We'll give you a card to record each TB dose, and the clinic nurse will check it every visit.
Put a new needle on the insulin pen every time, and remove it straight after injecting.
Hold the insulin pen in place for ten seconds after pressing, so the full dose goes in.
Salbutamol can make your hands shake or your heart beat faster for a short while. That's a common side effect.
Prednisolone might raise your sugar level a little, so check it more often while you're on the course.
Please take the amoxicillin three times a day, roughly every eight hours: morning, afternoon and bedtime.
One amoxicillin capsule is 500mg. Swallow it whole, and please don't open the capsule.
Paracetamol can be given with ibuprofen if the fever is stubborn, but space them a few hours apart.
Your mother's warfarin dose changed to 3mg today. The new instructions are written in the yellow booklet.
If you see blood in your urine or black stools while on warfarin, come to the emergency department.
Omeprazole capsules can be opened and sprinkled on a spoon of soft food if grandma finds them hard to swallow.
Ibuprofen isn't suitable for you because of your kidney function, so please stick to paracetamol only.
Losartan and perindopril shouldn't be taken together, so the doctor has stopped the perindopril.
For the sinusitis, doxycycline 100mg twice daily for one week. Avoid strong sunlight, because your skin may burn easily.
Don't take doxycycline with milk or antacids, because they stop it from being absorbed properly.
The budesonide nasal spray is two sprays in each nostril every morning. Aim slightly outward, away from the middle.
Clopidogrel and aspirin together increase bleeding risk, so tell any dentist or doctor that you're on both.
Uncle, do you know why you take the metformin? It helps your body use sugar better.
Before injecting, prime the pen with two units into the air to make sure the needle isn't blocked.
If your sugar is below four, don't inject your insulin yet. Have something sweet first and recheck.
Ventolin is your reliever. If you need it more than three times a week, your asthma isn't well controlled.
Let me write the times on the box for you: morning pill with breakfast, night pill after dinner.
This week you're on a reducing dose of prednisolone: four tablets, then three, then two, then one.
The azithromycin may give you a bit of diarrhoea. Drink plenty of fluids and it usually settles.
Please don't share your antibiotics with family members, even if they have similar symptoms.
Gliclazide 80mg, one tablet before breakfast and one before dinner. If you skip a meal, skip that tablet too.
The pharmacy has switched your atorvastatin to a different brand, but it's the same medicine and strength.
Rub the ibuprofen gel gently on the swollen knee three times a day, then wash your hands.
Auntie, you can crush the amlodipine and mix it with a spoon of porridge if the tablet is hard to swallow.
Keep your medicines in their original packets, in a cool, dry place out of the children's reach.
The metformin extended-release tablet must be swallowed whole. Please don't break or chew it.
Your blood pressure is 150 over 95 today, so the doctor has added losartan to your amlodipine.
For the urinary tract infection, take the antibiotic for five days and drink at least eight glasses of water daily.
Paracetamol for children is based on weight. At fifteen kilos, that's 7.5ml of the syrup each time.
Please don't give ibuprofen for dengue fever. Only paracetamol is safe, because of the bleeding risk.
Your mealtime insulin should be injected fifteen to thirty minutes before you eat, not after.
When travelling, carry your insulin in your hand luggage and never pack it in the checked bag.
Uncle, the perindopril is 4mg, once a day. Take it before breakfast.
This new tablet is for your heart failure, so you may pass urine more often in the first few hours.
Take the water tablet in the morning, so you're not waking up to go to the toilet all night.
Weigh yourself every morning while on these heart failure medicines, and write the number down.
If you feel very dizzy after the first dose of perindopril, lie down and raise your legs.
Here's a spacer for your Ventolin. It helps more medicine reach your lungs, especially during an attack.
During an asthma attack, take four puffs of Ventolin through the spacer, one puff at a time.
Your COPD inhaler is one puff once a day. Try to use it at the same time every morning.
Wash the spacer once a week in warm soapy water and let it air-dry. Don't wipe the inside with a cloth.
Omeprazole is fine for gastric pain, but if you need it every day for months, the doctor should review.
Okay auntie, for the next three days, take the prednisolone after breakfast, eight tablets at once.
The cough syrup is 10ml three times a day. Use the measuring cup, not a kitchen spoon.
Avoid alcohol while you're on the antibiotics, as it can make you feel sick and slow your recovery.
With metformin, your stomach may feel bloated at first. Taking it in the middle of a meal can help.
Your atorvastatin is 20mg now. The dose went up because your cholesterol was still high.
Please continue your clopidogrel after discharge. The next supply will come from your usual clinic.
The cetirizine is for the itchy nose and sneezing. One tablet a day is enough.
Paracetamol is safe alongside your blood pressure tablets, so you don't need to space them apart.
If Panadol isn't enough for the headache, don't add more tablets. Come back so we can review.
This insulin is the long-acting one, the grey pen, taken once at bedtime.
The orange pen is your mealtime insulin. You use it three times a day, before each main meal.
Don't mix up the two pens, ya. Grey at night, orange before meals.
Leave a new insulin pen out of the fridge for half an hour before injecting, so it stings less.
Check the insulin before use. The clear type should always look clear, never cloudy.
For the cloudy insulin, roll the pen gently between your palms ten times before injecting.
Your sugar reading this morning was fourteen. Increase your night insulin by two units, as the doctor said.
Grandma's warfarin must not be taken with ibuprofen. For pain, use paracetamol instead.
Green leafy vegetables affect warfarin. You don't need to avoid them, just keep the amount steady from week to week.
Please take the azithromycin one hour before food, or two hours after, for better absorption.
These tablets are prescribed for thirty days. Make sure you collect next month's supply before they finish.
The pharmacy can pack your supply into weekly pill boxes if that makes it easier for you.
Uncle, if you feel very tired and your muscles ache badly on atorvastatin, stop it and see the doctor.
Amlodipine can cause ankle swelling in some people. It's usually mild, but tell us if it bothers you.
Before taking any new medicine from outside, please check with the pharmacist because of your kidney condition.
For the bronchitis, the doctor didn't give antibiotics because it's likely viral. Rest and paracetamol are enough.
Give the oral rehydration solution in small sips every few minutes if your child keeps vomiting.
Don't add sugar or juice to the oral rehydration solution, because it changes the balance of salts.
Throw away any mixed rehydration solution after twenty-four hours and make a fresh batch.
Budesonide won't help during a sudden attack. It works slowly over weeks to calm the airways.
You should feel less wheezy after a couple of weeks on the preventer, so keep using it daily.
Prednisolone for your asthma flare is 40mg once a day for five days. No tapering needed.
Start the gout tablets as soon as the attack begins. The sooner you take them, the faster it settles.
After a heart stent, clopidogrel is usually needed for at least one year. Try not to miss a single dose.
Losartan can raise your potassium level, so we'll do a blood test in two weeks.
If your home reading is below 100 over 60 and you feel faint, skip that day's dose and call the clinic.
Your doctor wants you on paracetamol regularly for three days: two tablets, four times a day.
Can you tell me back how you'll take these? I just want to make sure it's clear.
This one is omeprazole 20mg, the small pink capsule. The white round one is your amlodipine.
Metformin can continue during a mild illness, but stop it if you're vomiting and can't keep fluids down.
On sick days, keep checking your sugar every four hours, even if you're not eating much.
Please don't stop your insulin when you're sick. You may even need more, so call the clinic for advice.
Take the cetirizine for one week, then stop and see whether the rash comes back.
For the upper respiratory tract infection, just paracetamol and plenty of warm fluids. Antibiotics won't help a virus.
If you're breastfeeding, paracetamol and amoxicillin are both safe for your baby.
Shake the azithromycin syrup well, then give 5ml once daily using the syringe provided.
Keep the amoxicillin syrup in the fridge after mixing. It's good for seven days.
Please take the doxycycline with lunch rather than at bedtime, so it doesn't irritate your throat.
You'll need to continue the TB medicine for six months. Stopping early can make the infection come back stronger.
If you forget a TB dose, take it later the same day. Never take two doses the next day.
After each Ventolin puff, hold your breath for about ten seconds, then breathe out slowly.
Your inhaler technique is good, uncle. Just slow down the breath in a little more.
For the pneumonia, you'll go home on amoxicillin 1g three times a day to complete ten days.
The first antibiotic dose was given here through the drip, so start the tablets tomorrow morning.
If you're planning to fast, talk to the doctor first, because the gliclazide dose may need changing.
Since you'll be fasting this month, we need to adjust your insulin timing. Let's go through it now.
Warfarin needs a regular blood test called INR. Your next one is in one week.
Warfarin reacts with some antibiotics, so always mention it whenever a doctor gives you new medicine.
Keep your Ventolin with you at all times, especially when you exercise or go outstation.
Take the ibuprofen for headache only when needed, and no more than three times a day.
Mild nausea with the antibiotic is common. Taking it with food usually helps.
Please finish the last two days of amoxicillin, even though the fever is gone.
Losartan can be taken with or without food; just be consistent every day.
If your lips or tongue swell after starting perindopril, that's serious. Go straight to the emergency department.
Atorvastatin is long term. Most people stay on it for life to protect the heart.
You can take the amlodipine and atorvastatin together at night if that's easier to remember.
There are six insulin pens in this box. Five go into the fridge, and one is for daily use.
Insulin that has been frozen should be thrown away, even if it looks normal after thawing.
Please do not inject into areas with lumps, because the insulin won't absorb well there.
Uphamol 650 is a stronger paracetamol. One tablet up to four times a day, not more.
At home, use the salbutamol nebuliser every four hours only if needed, with one full vial each time.
Omeprazole may cause a mild headache in the first week. That usually improves on its own.
If the prednisolone upsets your stomach, take it with a proper meal and continue the omeprazole.
For the itchy rash, apply the cream thinly twice a day and take the cetirizine at night.
Auntie, set a phone alarm for your medicines. It really helps with remembering the timing.
This clopidogrel is from a new supplier. The packaging looks different, but it's the same medicine.
Please let the doctor know about any supplements you take, as some can affect your blood thinner.
The azithromycin course is short, but the medicine keeps working in your body for about a week.
Metformin 1g after dinner only for now. If your sugar stays high, we'll add a breakfast dose.
For the COPD flare, prednisolone 30mg for five days, and use the nebuliser at home if needed.
Before using a new inhaler, spray two test puffs into the air to make sure it's working.
For the next two weeks, drink at least eight glasses of water a day, unless the doctor told you to limit fluids.
Keep the wound dry for the first forty-eight hours. After that you can shower, but pat it dry gently.
Auntie, reduce the salt in your cooking, and go easy on soy sauce, salted fish and instant noodles.
After the gastroenteritis, start with plain porridge, toast or biscuits, then slowly return to your normal diet.
Avoid oily and spicy food for a few days while your stomach recovers.
You can walk around the house, but no heavy lifting for at least six weeks after the operation.
With heart failure, limit your fluids to about one and a half litres a day, including soups and drinks.
Uncle, you're allowed to shower tomorrow. Just cover the dressing with plastic and tape down the edges.
Change the dressing every two days at the nearest clinic, or sooner if it gets wet or soaked through.
Rest as much as you need this week. Your body is still recovering from the pneumonia.
Please use your MC to rest at home; going back to work too early may set you back.
Do the breathing exercises three times a day: breathe in deeply through the nose, hold, then blow out slowly.
While recovering from dengue, keep drinking plenty of fluids like water, isotonic drinks and clear soups.
Keep your feet clean and dry, and check them every day for cuts or blisters, since you have diabetes.
Wear shoes or slippers at all times, even inside the house, to protect your feet.
Avoid sugary drinks like syrup, bubble tea and soft drinks. Plain water or unsweetened tea is better.
Half your plate should be vegetables, a quarter protein, and a quarter rice or noodles.
If you smoke, this is a good time to stop. The clinic runs a quit-smoking programme that can help.
Stay away from cigarette smoke and open burning, as both can trigger your asthma.
During haze season, keep the windows closed and wear a mask when you go outside.
Sleep with your head raised on two pillows if you feel breathless lying flat.
Rest your leg on a pillow when you sit down, to help the swelling go down.
For the gout, avoid organ meats and shellfish, and cut down on beer.
Drink more water to help flush out the uric acid, at least two litres a day.
After the stroke, your father will need help getting up. Always stay beside him when he walks.
Remove loose rugs and put a non-slip mat in the bathroom, so he doesn't fall.
Practise the arm and hand exercises the physiotherapist showed you, twice a day, about fifteen minutes each.
Feed him slowly with small spoonfuls, and make sure he's sitting upright while eating.
Thicken his drinks with the powder we gave you, because thin liquids may go down into the lungs.
For the urinary tract infection, drink plenty of water and don't hold your urine for too long.
Wipe from front to back after using the toilet, to reduce the chance of another infection.
For the sinusitis, a saline nasal rinse twice a day can help clear the blocked nose.
Steam inhalation over a bowl of hot water may ease the congestion, but be careful not to scald yourself.
Warm water with honey can soothe the cough, but don't give honey to babies under one year old.
Your child can go back to school once the fever has been gone for twenty-four hours without medicine.
Keep the baby's fluids up by breastfeeding more often, even if he takes less each time.
Wash your hands with soap before preparing food and after using the toilet, so the diarrhoea doesn't spread.
Use separate towels for each family member until the diarrhoea settles.
For TB, open the windows at home to let fresh air in, and cover your mouth when you cough.
During the first two weeks of TB treatment, try to sleep in a separate room if possible.
Weigh yourself every morning after the toilet and before breakfast, and write it in the book.
Cut down on processed foods like sausages, canned soups and salted eggs, because they're high in salt.
Check your blood pressure at home twice a day for a week and bring the readings to clinic.
Sit quietly for five minutes before measuring your blood pressure, with your arm resting on the table.
Check your sugar level before breakfast and two hours after dinner, and record both in the booklet.
Brisk walking for thirty minutes, five days a week, is good for both your sugar and your heart.
Start slowly with ten-minute walks, then build up as you feel stronger.
After a chest infection, you may feel tired for a few weeks. That's normal, so pace yourself.
You can return to light office work after one week, but avoid heavy work for a month.
No driving for at least one month after the stroke, until the doctor clears you.
Please don't soak the wound in a bathtub or swimming pool until the stitches are out.
Mild redness around the stitches is normal, but it should look better each day.
A little clear fluid from the wound on the first day is okay. Just replace the gauze.
Keep the cast dry by covering it with a plastic bag when you shower.
Put ice wrapped in a towel on the sprain for fifteen minutes, three or four times a day.
For the rash, avoid very hot showers and use a gentle, soap-free cleanser.
Cut your child's fingernails short so he doesn't scratch the itchy spots.
Wear loose cotton clothes to let the skin breathe while the rash heals.
Drink small amounts often rather than a big glass at once, if you're still feeling nauseous.
Avoid milk and dairy for a few days after the diarrhoea, as they may upset the stomach again.
Your fluid chart matters. Write down every cup you drink and each time you pass urine.
For heart failure, don't add salt at the table, and go easy on sauces and pickles.
Eat smaller meals more often if big meals make you breathless.
With COPD, stay active with gentle walks, and use pursed-lip breathing when you feel short of breath.
Get your flu vaccine every year, uncle, because chest infections hit COPD patients harder.
Use the home oxygen at two litres per minute, and keep it well away from the stove.
No smoking in the house at all while the oxygen is in use. It's a real fire risk.
Keep the nasal prongs clean and change the tubing every month.
For the sore throat, gargle with warm salt water three times a day.
Try to get at least seven hours of sleep, so your body can recover properly.
After dengue, clear any stagnant water around the house every week to stop mosquitoes breeding.
Use mosquito repellent and sleep under a net, so the rest of the family doesn't get dengue too.
Try to eat something every few hours, even just biscuits or fruit, to keep your energy up.
Take things slowly at home, auntie. The housework can wait until you feel stronger.
Ask your children to help with the marketing and cooking for the next two weeks.
If you're on insulin, always keep sweets or a small packet of juice in your bag.
Choose brown rice or wholemeal bread instead of white rice when you can.
Fruit is healthy, but keep sweet ones like durian, mango and rambutan to small portions.
A light dinner before eight o'clock can help keep your morning sugar down.
Please avoid long hot baths for now, as they can make you dizzy.
Get up slowly from lying down: sit on the edge of the bed first, then stand.
For the leg swelling, avoid standing for long hours and put your feet up when you rest.
Wear the compression stockings during the day and take them off at night.
Don't cross your legs when sitting, so the blood can flow freely.
For bronchitis, stay well hydrated. It helps loosen the phlegm so you can cough it out.
Turn your father every two hours in bed to prevent pressure sores.
Keep his skin clean and dry, especially around the back and hips.
A pillow between his knees when he's lying on his side will make him more comfortable.
At home you can bathe normally, but avoid scrubbing the old drip site on your hand.
The drip site may stay bruised for a few days. A warm compress can help.
Chew slowly and choose soft foods while your mouth ulcers are still painful.
For the constipation, add more fruit, vegetables and water to your daily diet.
A short walk after each meal helps your digestion and your sugar level.
Keep a small diary of what you eat and how you feel, so we can spot what triggers the gastric pain.
Avoid lying down for two hours after meals if you have reflux.
Raise the head of your bed slightly to reduce the heartburn at night.
Cut down on coffee, fizzy drinks and very spicy food to help with the reflux.
Please avoid alcohol completely while your liver recovers.
Your mother needs someone at home with her for the first few nights after discharge.
Keep a light on in the corridor at night so she doesn't trip on the way to the toilet.
Put her medicines in a weekly pill box, and have one family member check it each evening.
For the high fever at home, sponge him with lukewarm water, not cold water.
Dress your child in light clothing and keep the room airy while he has a fever.
Don't wrap the baby in thick blankets when she's feverish, because it traps the heat.
Give fluids in small amounts every fifteen minutes if your child is vomiting.
You can keep breastfeeding throughout the diarrhoea. It actually helps the baby recover.
Rest your voice for a few days and avoid shouting or whispering.
After the asthma attack, skip heavy exercise for a few days until the wheeze settles.
Wash the bedsheets and pillow covers in hot water weekly to reduce dust mites.
Keep the cat out of the bedroom if its fur triggers your son's asthma.
Your stitches will come out at the clinic in ten days. Until then, keep the area clean.
Apply a thin layer of the antibiotic ointment after cleaning the wound with saline.
Use cooled boiled water to clean the wound if you don't have saline at home.
For the first week, sleep on your back so you don't press on the wound.
Your appetite may be poor for a while. Small, nutritious snacks are better than forcing big meals.
Try to include eggs, fish, chicken or tofu at every meal to help the wound heal.
If you feel low or can't sleep after the stroke, please talk to us. Support is available.
Keep the stroke booklet handy. The exercises and warning signs are listed clearly inside.
Take the stairs slowly, uncle, and rest on the landing if you get breathless.
On long car rides, stop and walk around every hour to prevent clots in the legs.
If you have chest pain that spreads to your arm or jaw, call an ambulance straight away.
Come back immediately if the breathlessness gets worse or you can't finish a sentence.
Watch for bleeding gums, nosebleeds or black stools during dengue. Those need urgent attention.
If your child is very drowsy, hard to wake, or refusing all drinks, bring him to emergency at once.
Sudden weakness on one side of the face or body can mean a stroke. Go to the nearest emergency department.
If the fever goes above thirty-nine and won't come down with paracetamol, come back to see us.
Vomiting everything, even water, for more than six hours is a warning sign. Please come in.
Passing very little urine, or none for eight hours, may mean dehydration. Please return to the clinic.
If you see blood in the stool or it turns black, come to emergency immediately.
Severe tummy pain with dengue fever is dangerous. Don't wait at home; come straight to hospital.
If the Ventolin isn't helping and your chest still feels tight after twenty minutes, call for help.
Blue lips or fingertips mean you need oxygen urgently. Call an ambulance.
A sudden severe headache, worse than any you've had before, needs to be checked right away.
If your father becomes confused, sleepy or unusually agitated, bring him back immediately.
A sugar reading below four that doesn't improve after sweets is an emergency.
If your sugar is above twenty and you're vomiting or breathing fast, go to emergency.
Coughing up blood is not normal. Please come in the same day.
Leg swelling with pain, redness and warmth in one calf needs urgent review.
If you gain more than two kilos in two days, call the heart failure nurse or come in.
Palpitations with fainting or chest pain are serious. Don't drive yourself; call for an ambulance.
Watch the wound for pus, spreading redness or a bad smell. Those are signs of infection.
If you get fever with back pain and shivering during the UTI, come back right away.
If your lips, eyes or throat swell after a new medicine, go to emergency immediately.
If her breathing becomes noisy or the skin between her ribs sucks in, bring her in straight away.
Babies under three months with any fever above thirty-eight must see a doctor the same day.
If the diarrhoea has blood or mucus, or lasts more than three days, please come back.
If you faint, or you can't stand up without falling, you need to be seen urgently.
A stiff neck with high fever and a severe headache must be checked immediately.
If the chest pain comes on at rest and lasts more than ten minutes, don't wait. Call an ambulance.
Sudden slurred speech or trouble understanding words is a stroke warning. Every minute counts.
Remember FAST: face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty, time to call an ambulance.
If a cut won't stop bleeding after ten minutes of pressure while you're on warfarin, come to emergency.
Uncle, if your urine turns dark like tea and you feel very weak, come in immediately.
When the dengue fever settles, days three to seven are the critical phase, so watch closely for warning signs.
Cold, clammy hands and feet during dengue could mean the blood pressure is dropping. Come straight in.
If your child hasn't passed urine for six hours, she may be dehydrated. Please bring her back.
Sunken eyes, a dry mouth and no tears when crying are signs of dehydration in children.
If your heart is racing and it doesn't settle after twenty minutes of rest, come in.
Wheezing that wakes you at night more than once a week means we need to review your asthma soon.
If your ankles swell up suddenly and you can't lie flat, come to the hospital.
Waking up gasping for breath at night is a warning sign that the heart failure is getting worse.
If the TB medicine makes your eyes or skin turn yellow, stop and come to the clinic urgently.
New confusion in an elderly person can be a sign of infection. Don't just assume it's old age.
Fits or seizures, even a short one, need to be assessed in the emergency department.
If the vomit is green or has blood in it, please come to emergency straight away.
Severe pain in the big toe with a fever may not be just gout. Come back if you feel unwell.
If you feel your throat closing up or you can't swallow your saliva, that's an emergency.
Tell us immediately if the drip site becomes swollen, painful or starts leaking.
A high fever that keeps coming back after five days needs another check, even if you feel okay in between.
If your cough is getting worse after two weeks, or you're losing weight, please come back for review.
